title: Absorbed in Inertia: Activation Analysis for Computer-Use Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.37176v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Computer-use agents have become increasingly capable of executing tasks on live desktops through natural-language instructions, based on trajectories of screenshots, actions, and reasoning. We discover that they can stealthily exhibit inertia, in which they repeat fruitless actions despite recognizing that these actions are ineffective. We hypothesize that inertia is reflected in the agent's internal state, i.e., the activation values of the agent's underlying model, and propose a protocol to measure the relationship between the two. Extensive analysis of high-dimensional activation states shows that inertia corresponds to an absorbing region of activation space, where activation values become stale across actions and even after attempts to steer them. tldr: 该论文发现计算机使用智能体会隐蔽地陷入“惯性”而重复无效操作，并证明惯性对应于激活空间中的吸收区域，进而提出通过重新初始化激活值来摆脱惯性的R³（重置、重新路由、恢复）方法。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that computer-use agents can stealthily exhibit inertia by repeating fruitless actions, shows that inertia corresponds to an absorbing region of activation space, and proposes R³ (Reset, Reroute, Restore), which escapes inertia by drastically re-initializing the agent's activations.
